title: Record-Save Order of Execution
objectives: Place before-save Flows, before triggers, validation, duplicate rules, the save, and after triggers in the official relative order.
Explain workflow field-update re-entry: what reruns once and what does not.
Distinguish same-row before work from after-save related DML and post-commit async work.
Use the official sequence to debug recursion and skipped automation without inventing a personal order.
diagnostic_question: An after-save Flow updates the same Opportunity, and a workflow field update also writes a field. Which steps can re-enter, which steps are skipped on recursive saves, and where would you look first in the official order?
definition: Record-save order of execution is the server-side sequence Salesforce runs when a record is inserted, updated, or upserted—including before-save flows, before triggers, system and custom validation, duplicate rules, the database save, after triggers, assignment/auto-response/workflow/escalation automations, after-save flows, roll-up recalculation, sharing evaluation, commit, and post-commit work. ([Triggers and Order of Execution](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_triggers_order_of_execution.htm))
why_it_matters: Most 'automation ran twice' or 'validation never fired' incidents are order-of-execution misunderstandings—especially workflow re-entry, recursive save skip windows, and before-save versus after-save placement. Interviewers want the official page, not a memorized unofficial blog.
sixty_second_explanation: A save is a factory paint line with fixed stations. Before-save Flow paints first, then Apex before triggers, then validation and duplicate rules, then the row is hung on the rack (saved, not shipped). After triggers run, then assignment, auto-response, workflow, escalation, after-save Flow, roll-ups, sharing, commit (the truck leaves), then email and async. Workflow field updates send the piece back through before/after update triggers once without re-running custom validation or Flows on that replay. Always reopen the Apex Developer Guide for the API version under discussion.
deeper_explanation: The authoritative list lives on Triggers and Order of Execution and is versioned. Headline relative order used in interviews: original record loaded, new values applied, system validation, before-save record-triggered Flows, before triggers, custom validation, duplicate rules, save (not committed), after triggers, assignment/auto-response/workflow/processes/escalation, after-save Flows, entitlements/roll-ups/criteria-based sharing, commit, post-commit email and async. If a step's exact current wording is unclear, mark Needs verification and open the page. ([Triggers and Order of Execution](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_triggers_order_of_execution.htm))

Trigger events versus record state still apply inside that pipeline (APEX-008): before triggers see unsaved Trigger.new (writable, no insert Id); after triggers see saved read-only rows with Id. Before-save Flow is earlier than before triggers and is same-row only.

Workflow field updates cause one additional before/after update trigger pass. Custom validation rules, duplicate rules, and Flows do not rerun on that replay—a frequent interview trap. Recursive saves skip a documented window (assignment through grandparent roll-up processing). Reverify the skip-window wording on the current page.

After-save Flow or after-trigger DML on the same row re-enters the pipeline and must be idempotent. Post-commit async sees committed data and uses a new governor pool (APEX-007/011). Multiple Apex triggers on one event remain unordered (APEX-008).

mental_model.analogy: A factory paint line with fixed stations: you cannot swap the primer booth with the shipping dock.
useful_mapping: before-save Flow → first primer booth (same piece, before Apex before triggers)
before trigger → detail sanding while the piece is still on the hook (Trigger.new writable)
validation / duplicate rules → quality gate before it is hung as saved
database save → hung on the rack (Id exists, not yet on the truck)
after trigger → tag other parts now that the barcode exists
workflow extra pass → one authorized rework loop through sanding booths, skipping some gates
post-commit async → a later shift with its own time clock
where_it_breaks: The official list has more stations than a simple paint line (entitlements, sharing, escalation).
Workflow re-entry is not a general 'run everything twice' loop.
Gallery flowcharts can lag the Developer Guide.
The analogy does not encode governor numbers.

telugu_glossary.telugu: Fixed station order when a record saves.
One extra before/after trigger pass after a workflow field update.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Order of execution is the save pipeline: before-save Flow, before triggers, validation, save, after triggers, then assignment/workflow/after-save Flow, roll-ups, sharing, commit, post-commit async. Workflow field updates get one extra before/after update pass without re-running custom validation or Flows.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I treat the Apex Developer Guide as source of truth. Same-row work belongs in before-save Flow or before triggers; Id-dependent work belongs after save. I call out workflow re-entry and the recursive-save skip window. Multiple Apex triggers are unordered and share governors. Post-commit async sees committed data and a new limit pool. If I am unsure of a numbered step, I say so and open the page rather than invent a station.

terminology.plain: The fixed server sequence used while saving a record.
terminology.precise: The documented series of steps for insert/update/upsert for a given API version, from load through commit and post-commit work.
terminology.example: Before-save Flow runs before before triggers in current docs.
terminology.non_example: A team coding-style order for handler methods.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Flow trigger-order values—they order Flows among themselves, not the whole pipeline.
terminology.boundary: The Developer Guide page beats gallery diagrams if they disagree.

terminology.plain: A Flow that updates the triggering record before it is written.
terminology.precise: Record-triggered Flow configured to run before save; executes before Apex before triggers; same-record updates only.
terminology.example: Stamp Status on Case before insert.
terminology.non_example: Creating related Tasks—that is after save.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Before Apex trigger: later than before-save Flow.
terminology.boundary: Same-row only; no related-record DML in before-save Flow.

terminology.plain: Apex that runs before the record is saved.
terminology.precise: Trigger.new is writable; addError can block; insert Id is not available yet.
terminology.example: Normalize a phone on Contact before insert.
terminology.non_example: Inserting children that need the parent Id.

terminology.plain: Apex that runs after save and before commit.
terminology.precise: Id exists; Trigger.new is read-only; related DML is typical and can re-enter the pipeline.
terminology.example: Create a related Task after Case insert.
terminology.non_example: Mutating Trigger.new fields in after context.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Post-commit async: after commit, new transaction.
terminology.boundary: Must be idempotent if it updates the same row.

terminology.plain: The one extra update pass workflow field updates can cause.
terminology.precise: Salesforce updates the record again, re-runs system validations, and fires before/after update triggers one additional time only—without re-running custom validation, duplicate rules, or Flows on that replay.
terminology.example: A workflow sets a checkbox and your before-update trigger runs a second time.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Recursive save skip window—a different official nuance.
terminology.boundary: Memorize what does versus does not rerun.

terminology.plain: Commit makes the save durable; post-commit work runs afterward.
terminology.precise: After sharing evaluation, DML commits; then email, enqueued async Apex, and asynchronous Flow paths can run against committed state.
terminology.example: Queueable enqueued from an after trigger runs after commit.
terminology.non_example: Assuming a future method sees uncommitted rows from the original save.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Save-without-commit earlier (Ids exist, rollback still possible).
terminology.boundary: Post-commit failures do not roll back the original save.

mcqs.prompt: In current docs, when do before-save record-triggered Flows run relative to Apex before triggers?
mcqs.rationale: The order-of-execution page places before-save Flows before before triggers.

mcqs.prompt: On a workflow field-update replay, which reruns?

options.A: Before and after update triggers (one additional time)
options.B: Custom validation, duplicate rules, and Flows
options.C: The entire pipeline including assignment forever

mcqs.rationale: Workflow field updates cause one extra before/after update trigger pass and do not rerun custom validation, duplicate rules, or Flows on that replay.

distractor_explanations.B: Those are the skipped items on the replay.
distractor_explanations.C: It is one extra pass, not an infinite loop.

mcqs.prompt: After the database save but before commit, after triggers see what record state?

options.C: The row is already post-commit async

mcqs.rationale: Save assigns Id; after-trigger records are read-only (APEX-008 rules inside the pipeline).

mcqs.prompt: Where should same-row field updates go if Flow can do them?

options.A: Before-save Flow, which runs before before triggers

mcqs.rationale: Before-save Flow is the official early same-row station.

distractor_explanations.B: After-save is for work that needs Id or other records.

mcqs.prompt: Is the after-trigger save already committed?

options.A: No. Commit is a later station; rollback is still possible

mcqs.rationale: Id exists after save; commit is after sharing evaluation.

distractor_explanations.D: The pipeline is for insert/update/upsert primarily.

mcqs.prompt: An after trigger updates the same record and assignment rules do not fire again. First check?

options.A: Recursive-save skip window on the official page
options.D: Whether Apex public equals Java public

mcqs.rationale: Recursive saves skip a documented window that includes assignment through roll-up processing.

mcqs.prompt: Who wins if a blog and the Developer Guide disagree on order?

options.A: Triggers and Order of Execution for the API version

mcqs.rationale: This lesson treats the official page as authoritative.

mcqs.prompt: Multiple after-update Apex triggers on one object:

options.A: Order is not guaranteed; they still share governors
options.B: They run in filename order as a documented contract

mcqs.rationale: APEX-008 rule still holds inside the after-trigger station.

mcqs.prompt: Need a callout that must see committed Opportunity data?

options.A: Enqueue async after the after trigger; it runs post-commit
options.D: Call out while DML is pending in the same trigger without care

mcqs.rationale: Post-commit async sees committed data and a new pool. Callout-with-pending-DML is a neighbor constraint.

mcqs.prompt: Custom validation runs where relative to before triggers in the usual insert/update path?

options.A: After before triggers and before the save

mcqs.rationale: The documented sequence places custom validation after before triggers and before the database save.

distractor_explanations.D: Custom validation does not rerun on workflow replay.

mcqs.prompt: Which statement separates order-of-execution metadata from business data?

options.A: Deploying a trigger or Flow does not insert Opportunities; a save of a LAB_ row runs the pipeline
options.B: The order-of-execution page is an Opportunity record

mcqs.rationale: Automations are metadata. The saved row is data.

distractor_explanations.C: Commit commits DML, not metadata deploy.

mcqs.prompt: Before-save Flow versus before trigger for a simple same-row stamp?

options.A: Prefer before-save Flow when it fits; it runs earlier than the before trigger
options.B: Always write a global Apex trigger first

mcqs.rationale: AUTO-001 plus official order: before-save Flow is the earlier same-row station.

interview_questions.question: Walk record-save order of execution at interview speed.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Before-save Flow, before triggers, validation and duplicate rules, save, after triggers, assignment/auto-response/workflow/escalation, after-save Flow, roll-ups and sharing, commit, post-commit async. I reopen the official page for the numbered list.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I stress relative order more than memorizing twenty bullets. I place before-save Flow before Apex before triggers. I separate save from commit. I mention workflow re-entry and recursive skip as the traps. I refuse blog order if it conflicts with Triggers and Order of Execution.
interview_questions.example: Opportunity UI save: Flow stamps a field, before trigger uppercases NextStep, validation runs, then after trigger creates a Task.
tradeoffs: Memorize headlines vs open the page
Flow vs Apex at each station
weak_answer_warnings: Apex before Flow as a universal rule

interview_questions.question: How do trigger events versus record state sit inside that order?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: The before-trigger station still has writable Trigger.new and no insert Id. The after-trigger station has Id and read-only Trigger.new. Order of execution tells you when those stations run.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I do not re-teach all of APEX-008, but I connect them. Before-save Flow is even earlier than the before-trigger station. After-save Flow is later than after triggers. Commit is later still. Mixing those four names is the usual fail.
interview_questions.example: Child insert belongs in the after-trigger station, not in before-save Flow.

interview_questions.question: A workflow field update made your before-update trigger run twice. Did validation run twice?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Triggers yes, once extra. Custom validation, duplicate rules, and Flows do not rerun on that replay.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: This is the classic trap. I cite the order-of-execution workflow note. I make the trigger idempotent so the second pass is safe. I do not add a second Flow 'to catch the replay.' I distinguish this from a recursive after-trigger update, which uses the skip window instead.
interview_questions.example: Workflow sets LAB_WF__c; before-update debug prints twice; validation CODE_UNIT appears once.
tradeoffs: Keep workflow vs move the field update to Flow
Idempotent trigger vs blocking the second pass
follow_ups: Does process builder still appear in some orgs?

interview_questions.question: An after-save Flow updates the same Opportunity and assignment did not run again. What do you check?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Recursive-save skip window. Assignment through roll-up processing can be skipped. Confirm on the current page.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I look at the debug log for a second save without assignment CODE_UNIT. I ask whether this was a recursive update, not a new UI edit. I mark the exact skipped stations as needs verification if I cannot see the page. I do not 'fix' it by adding a second assignment rule.
interview_questions.example: After-save Flow writes a field; assignment rule stays quiet on the re-save.
tradeoffs: Same-row after-save Flow vs before-save Flow
Accept skip vs redesign so the first pass assigns
follow_ups: What is the current skip list?

interview_questions.question: Where do you put same-row work versus related DML versus callouts?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Same-row: before-save Flow or before trigger. Related DML: after trigger or after-save Flow. Callouts that need commit: post-commit async.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I draw three buckets on the whiteboard. I refuse after-trigger field stamps on Trigger.new. I refuse before-insert children. I refuse HTTP from before insert. I keep governors in mind because every station shares the pool until commit, then async gets a new pool.
interview_questions.example: Stamp Stage in before-save Flow; Task in after-save Flow; pricing callout in Queueable.
tradeoffs: Flow vs Apex at each bucket
follow_ups: What if after-save Flow hits limits?
weak_answer_warnings: One after trigger that does all three

interview_questions.question: Save versus commit—why do interviewers care?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Save creates the Id and still can roll back. Commit is later, after sharing evaluation. Async after commit sees durable data.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I use it to explain why after triggers can still fail the user-facing save, why future methods do not see uncommitted rows, and why post-commit email failures do not undo the Opportunity. I connect LimitException in an after trigger to a full rollback (APEX-006/007).
interview_questions.example: After trigger throws; the Opportunity insert the user thought succeeded is rolled back.
tradeoffs: Work in after trigger vs post-commit
User-visible failure vs eventual job failure
follow_ups: Do emails roll back the save if they fail?

interview_questions.question: Debug log shows your before trigger before a before-save Flow. What is going on?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Either you are misreading CODE_UNIT names, looking at a different update, or the Flow is after-save. Officially before-save Flow is first. Open the Flow's start and the official page.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I do not invent a new order. I check the Flow is actually before-save. I check I am not looking at the workflow replay's before trigger. I check packages. If the live page and the log still disagree, I treat that as needs verification—not as a chance to rewrite the handbook from a single org.
interview_questions.example: An after-save Flow labeled mentally as 'before save' by the admin.
tradeoffs: Trust the page vs trust one log
follow_ups: How do you filter debug logs to one save?
weak_answer_warnings: Declaring the official page wrong from one screenshot

interview_questions.question: How do you stay honest when the numbered list is long and versioned?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I memorize relative order and the two re-entry traps. I cite Triggers and Order of Execution and I say Needs verification for skip-window details I have not just read.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: That is the handbook standard. I will not recite an unofficial 21-step blog. I will draw before-save Flow, before trigger, validation, save, after trigger, workflow, after-save Flow, commit, async. I will connect APEX-008 record state. I will not invent governor numbers while drawing the line.
interview_questions.example: Whiteboard with eight boxes and a 'reverify' star on the skip window.
follow_ups: What changed when before-save Flow was introduced?
Where does Flow trigger order 1–2000 fit?
